tidal_locking.text: The Moon spins once for each trip around Earth (27.3 days), so the same side always faces us. Over time libration lets us see about 59% of the surface.

source.title: NASA Science: Moon facts

lunar_day.text: Sunrise to sunrise on the Moon takes about 29.5 Earth days, so the line between day and night sweeps around the Moon once a month.

source.title: NASA Science: Moon phases

light_time.text: The Moon is about 384,400 km away on average. Radio travels at the speed of light, so a call takes about 1.3 seconds each way.

source.title: NASA Science: Moon facts

pole_sun.text: At the south pole the Sun never climbs more than about 1.5 degrees above a flat horizon, because the Moon's spin axis is tilted only about 1.5 degrees.

source.title: JPL Horizons API

sun_year.text: Averaged over a year, a spot on Shackleton's rim gets sunlight about 86% of the time and Malapert about 73% (published Kaguya and LOLA studies).

source.title: Glaser et al. 2018, Illumination conditions at the lunar poles, Planetary and Space Science

psr_cold.text: Craters that never see the Sun are some of the coldest spots measured in the solar system: LRO measured below -246 C there. NASA's Moon Base page gives about -203 C for shadowed craters in general.

source.title: NASA Science: Weather on the Moon

sources.title: NASA Science: Weather on the Moon

psr_cold.checked: 2026-11-14: science.nasa.gov 'lower than -410°F (-246°C)'; nasa.gov/reference/moonbase-about 'as low as -334°F (-203°C) inside permanently shadowed craters'. Replaces Paige et al. 2010's -235 C (an early Diviner result).

artemis_timeline.text: Artemis II flew its crew around the Moon in April 2026. In February 2026 NASA made Artemis III a 2027 test flight in Earth orbit. Artemis IV, planned for early 2028, is to land two astronauts near the south pole.

source.title: NASA: Artemis IV

sources.title: NASA Adds Mission to Artemis Lunar Program, Updates Architecture (Feb 27, 2026)

artemis_timeline.checked: 2026-11-14: Artemis IV page launch 'Early 2028', 'two crew members will descend to the surface ... near the South Pole'; Feb 27 release: Artemis III 'now in 2027', tests 'in low Earth orbit'.

landing_regions.text: NASA's October 2024 list has 9 candidate landing regions near the south pole, including Malapert Massif and de Gerlache Rim 2. Peak near Shackleton and Connecting Ridge were on the 2022 list but not the 2024 one.

source.title: NASA Provides Update on Artemis III Moon Landing Regions (Oct 2024)

apollo13_record.text: Artemis II passed Apollo 13's record of 248,655 miles from Earth on April 6, 2026.

source.title: NASA: Artemis II crew eclipses record for farthest human spaceflight

integrity_name.text: The Artemis II crew proposed the names Integrity and Carroll for two unnamed craters. As of November 2026 the IAU has not approved them.

source.title: USGS/IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Moon

integrity_name.checked: 2026-11-14: the Gazetteer's Moon list (newest approvals Sep 21, 2026) has no Integrity or Carroll.

orion_shelter.text: On Orion, a radiation sensor called HERA gives the crew up to 1 hour of warning. They pack into the floor bays behind stowage bags and can stay up to 24 hours.

source.title: NASA: Orion crew systems

artemis1_shielding.text: On Artemis I, test dummies showed the best-shielded spot in Orion got about 4 times less dose than the least shielded spot.

source.title: DLR: Orion radiation protection tested, Artemis I findings (2024)

sep_timing.text: After a big flare, solar particles can arrive in tens of minutes to a few hours. A CME cloud takes about 1 to 3 days.

source.title: NOAA SWPC: Coronal mass ejections

lcross.text: The LCROSS Centaur, about 2,300 kg, hit Cabeus crater in 2009. Its plume held about 155 kg of water, about 5.6% of the soil by mass. The crater was about 25 to 30 m wide.

source.title: Colaprete et al. 2010, Detection of water in the LCROSS ejecta plume, Science 330

ice_distance.text: Straight-line distance from each outpost site to the middle of Shackleton crater, computed from the site coordinates: Shackleton Rim about 10 km, Malapert Massif about 130 km.
ice_distance.computed: great circle on a 1737.4 km sphere from mission/sites.json lat/lon to Shackleton (IAU 5450: -89.67, 129.78): 10.5 km and 128.7 km

source.title: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Shackleton

game_rules.text: Game doses are doubled so storms matter in 10 days. The powered shields, the greenhouse, the rim power cable and the relay satellite are pretend tech for the game.

source.title: Outpost Luna radiation data and game assumptions

artemis2_record.text: On April 6, 2026, Artemis II reached 252,756 miles from Earth, a new record for human spaceflight. It passed Apollo 13's record of 248,655 miles.

source.title: NASA: Artemis II Flight Day 6 lunar flyby updates

artemis2_record.checked: 2026-11-14: 'reached the mission's maximum distance from Earth at 252,756 miles, setting a new record for human spaceflight'.

moon_base.text: NASA plans its Moon Base, humanity's first lunar outpost, near the lunar South Pole. Phase One, robotic exploration, runs from now to 2029.

source.title: NASA: About the Moon Base

moon_base.checked: 2026-11-14: 'plans to establish the Moon Base near the lunar South Pole'; 'Phase One (Now–2029)'. Outpost Luna is a pretend base.

lro_crater.text: LRO launched on June 18, 2009. Its CRaTER instrument measures cosmic rays from the Sun and deep space.

source.title: NASA Science: LRO science and data

sources.title: NASA Science: LRO science and data

lro_crater.checked: 2026-11-14: launch 'June 18, 2009'; CRaTER 'measuring galactic and solar cosmic ray radiation'.

moon_phases.text: The Sun always lights half of the Moon. As the Moon goes around Earth, we see more or less of that sunlit half.

source.title: NASA Science: Moon phases

moon_phases.checked: 2026-11-14: 'The Sun always illuminates half of the Moon'.

lunar_eclipse.text: In a lunar eclipse, Earth gets in the way of the Sun's light, and Earth's shadow covers the Moon. It can look reddish.

source.title: NASA Space Place: What is an eclipse?

lunar_eclipse.checked: 2026-11-14: 'Earth gets in the way of the Sun's light hitting the Moon'; 'The Moon can also look reddish'.

moon_gravity.text: Gravity on the Moon's surface is 0.165 of Earth's, about one sixth. So 30 kg feels like about 5 kg.

source.title: NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet

feather_drop.text: At the end of the last Apollo 15 moonwalk in 1971, Commander David Scott dropped a hammer and a feather. They hit the ground together.

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo 15 Hammer-Feather Drop

feather_drop.checked: 2026-11-14: 'Commander David Scott'; they 'strike the lunar surface simultaneously'. Apollo 15 flew in 1971 (NSSDCA).

regolith.text: The Moon's dusty, rocky top layer is called regolith. Its tiny, sharp bits act like broken glass and cling to everything.

source.title: NASA Knows: What is lunar regolith? (grades 5-8)

regolith.checked: 2026-11-14: 'This dusty, rocky layer is called lunar regolith'; 'tiny, sharp pieces that can act like little bits of broken glass'.
